mainTopic: Whether riding an animal acquires it, compared to leading it, and whether holding the reins acquires
overview: רב יהודה remembers that שמואל ruled about riding (רכוב) and leading (מנהיג) an animal: one acquires it and one does not, but he forgot which is which. Since leading clearly acquires, the גמרא explains that his real question was about one person riding while another leads. רב יהודה tries to solve it from a משנה in כלאים about the person sitting in a wagon. In שמואל's version, the חכמים exempt the sitter, so riding is not a real act and does not acquire. אביי questions who said this proof. The גמרא then shows that holding the reins (מוסירה) does not make a rider different, because reins only work when an owner hands an animal over, not for a found or ownerless animal. Our משנה of two riders seems to prove that a rider does acquire. The גמרא answers that the rider there is driving the animal with his legs, and that he and the one leading are equal. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a new proof from a ברייתא about pulling a camel or driving a donkey, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יהודה half-remembers two rulings from שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה heard two rulings from שמואל about riding and leading an animal. One acquires and one does not, but he does not remember which is which.
steps.simpleTranslation: I heard two rulings from שמואל about one who rides an animal and one who leads it. In one case he acquires it and in the other he does not. But I don't know which ruling goes with which case.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה reports a ruling of his teacher שמואל but admits he forgot which half goes with which case. This sets up the whole discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both riding and leading are ways a person might try to take ownership of an animal. רב יהודה knows that only one of them works, and he cannot match the ruling to the case. The גמרא will now try to figure out what he could have been unsure about.

keyTerms.meaning: One who rides or sits on an animal
One who leads or drives an animal

phrases.english: I heard two rulings from Master Shmuel:
one who rides and one who leads an animal,
one acquires and one does not acquire.
But I do not know which of them is which.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of riding versus leading as a קנין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of riding and leading an animal, one acquires and one does not; רב יהודה does not remember which.

steps.title: How could there be any doubt? Leading clearly acquires
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רב יהודה meant. If he meant riding alone and leading alone, there should be no doubt: everyone agrees leading acquires, so only riding could fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? If you say one person only rides and another only leads, is there anyone who says that leading alone does not acquire? If any case does not acquire, it must be riding!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case רב יהודה could have been unsure about. It shows that the simple reading makes no sense, because leading is a well-known way to acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leading an animal is a standard קנין, so no one would say it fails. That means riding must be the one that does not acquire, and רב יהודה would have had no reason to be confused. So the case must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? (what exact case?)
If you say (introduces a reading that will be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying riding never acquires. It is only saying that if one of the two fails, it would obviously be riding, so there would be nothing to forget.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say one rides by himself and one leads by himself,
then about leading by itself,

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא מַאן דְּאָמַר לָא קָנֵי?
phrases.english: is there anyone who says he does not acquire?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר דְּלָא קָנֵי –
phrases.english: Rather, if there is a case where one could say he does not acquire,
it is riding where one could say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא רָכוּב לְחוֹדֵיהּ וּמַנְהִיג לְחוֹדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case רב יהודה's doubt could refer to, and rejects the simple reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact case was רב יהודה unsure about, given that leading alone clearly acquires?
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of רב יהודה's doubt as riding alone versus leading alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leading is an accepted קנין, so only riding could fail, leaving no room for doubt.

steps.title: The real question: one rides while another leads
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב יהודה's doubt was about one person riding while another leads the same animal. Does the rider win because he holds the animal, or the leader because the animal moves because of him?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his question was about a rider when there is also a leader. What is the law? Does the rider win, since he is holding onto the animal? Or perhaps the leader wins, since the animal walks because of him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case: two people competing for the same animal, one riding and one leading. It lays out the reason each might be stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the doubt makes sense: both acts work alone, but we need to know which is stronger when they compete. The rider has physical grip on the animal, while the leader is the one making it move. Whichever is stronger acquires, and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: In the place of, when there is also
He had a question / was unsure

steps.whatToRemember: The question is not whether riding or leading works alone, but which one wins when one person rides and another leads the same animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the question from 'does riding acquire?' to 'which act is stronger when both happen at once?', which is what the rest of the discussion will try to answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רָכוּב בִּמְקוֹם מַנְהִיג אִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Rather, he was unsure about a rider when someone else is leading.
What is the law?
Is the rider stronger, since he is holding onto it,
or perhaps the leader is stronger,
since it walks because of him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רָכוּב בִּמְקוֹם מַנְהִיג אִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by giving a new case where the doubt makes sense.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubt is about a rider and a leader competing at the same time, and which of them acquires.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubt was about riding alone versus leading alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt is which act is stronger when both happen together.

steps.title: רב יהודה tries to solve it from a משנה about leading mixed animals
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that רב יהודה tried to work it out himself from a משנה: when mixed animals pull a wagon, both the leader and the one sitting in the wagon get forty lashes, but רבי מאיר exempts the one sitting in the wagon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב יהודה told me, let us figure it out ourselves, as we learned in a משנה: The one who leads gets forty lashes, and the one sitting in the wagon gets forty lashes. רבי מאיר exempts the one sitting in the wagon.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה starts trying to solve his own question by quoting a משנה about leading two kinds of animals together. The גמרא is setting up a comparison between that case and rider versus leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, both the leader and the one sitting in the wagon are treated as 'leading' the animals, according to the first opinion. רבי מאיר disagrees and says the one sitting did nothing. This disagreement about whether sitting counts like leading will be used to decide the rider question.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see / figure it out ourselves
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר לִי רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Rav Yehuda said to me:
Let us see for ourselves,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: כלאים 8:3, about two different kinds of animals pulling a wagon together (דברים 22:10).

phrases.english: The one who leads receives the forty lashes,
and the one sitting in the wagon receives the forty lashes.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר פּוֹטֵר אֶת הַיּוֹשֵׁב בַּקָּרוֹן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir exempts the one sitting in the wagon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר לִי רַב יְהוּדָה: נֶחְזֵי אֲנַן, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attempt to answer the question of step 3 from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a rider or a leader is stronger for acquiring an animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כלאים about the leader and the one sitting in the wagon, with רבי מאיר's dissent

steps.title: The proof is completed: riding does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: Because שמואל's version of the משנה gives the exemption of the wagon-sitter to the חכמים, we learn that riding alone does not acquire. Riding while another person leads certainly does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since שמואל switched the opinions and taught that the חכמים exempt the one sitting in the wagon, we learn that riding alone does not acquire. All the more so, riding while someone else leads does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יהודה's proof and draws the conclusion. Sitting or riding is not a real action, so the rider does not acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's version of the משנה, the opinion that the wagon-sitter did nothing belongs to the חכמים, and we usually follow the חכמים. So sitting on or in something pulled by an animal is not a meaningful action. If riding alone does not acquire, then riding while someone else leads, which is the exact doubt from step 3, surely does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Switched or reversed (the names of who holds which opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: Riding does not acquire, according to רב יהודה's reading of שמואל. So when one person rides and another leads, the leader acquires.

phrases.english: And since שמואל reversed it and taught:
phrases.notes: In the משנה, רבי מאיר exempts the sitter. שמואל switched the names, so that opinion belongs to the חכמים, and we usually follow them.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis exempt the one sitting in the wagon,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ רָכוּב לְחוֹדֵיהּ לָא קָנֵי,
phrases.english: conclude from it: one who rides by himself does not acquire,
and all the more so one who rides while there is someone leading.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ רָכוּב לְחוֹדֵיהּ לָא קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that began in step 4 with the wagon משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Riding does not acquire, so in the case of one rider and one leader, the rider does not acquire.

steps.title: אביי questions who really said this proof
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that רב יוסף used to present this proof as his own reasoning. He never said it in the name of רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Didn't you tell us many times, 'Let us figure it out ourselves,' and you never told it to us in the name of רב יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the attribution, meaning who the proof came from. He is not challenging the proof itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב יוסף taught this proof as his own analysis ("let us see"). Now he says it came from רב יהודה. אביי wants to know which is true.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see (figure it out) ourselves

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Didn't you tell us many times:
"Let us see for ourselves,"
phrases.notes: In other words, רב יוסף used to bring the wagon proof as his own idea.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרְתְּ לַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: and you did not tell it to us in the name of Rav Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions who the proof in steps 4-5 came from.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the proof came from רב יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף had always presented this proof as his own reasoning, so how can it be רב יהודה's?

steps.title: רב יוסף confirms it was רב יהודה's proof and recalls his own question
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף insists the proof really was רב יהודה's. As evidence, he remembers the question he asked רב יהודה: a rider holds the reins, but a wagon-sitter does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Truly! And I also remember that I said to him: How can the master learn riding from sitting? The one sitting in the wagon does not hold the reins, but the rider holds the reins!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי: yes, it was רב יהודה's proof, and he even remembers the conversation. Inside his answer he repeats a challenge he once raised, which sets up רב יהודה's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Remembering his own question shows that the conversation with רב יהודה really happened. The question itself is a strong one. A rider on an animal usually holds the reins, which might count as an action of taking. A wagon passenger does not hold them, so the two cases may not be the same.

phrases.english: He said to him: Indeed!
And I also remember that I said to him:
How can the master resolve riding from sitting?
One sitting in the wagon does not hold the reins,
one riding the animal holds the reins!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִבְרָא! וּדְכִירְנָא נָמֵי דַּאֲמַרִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge about who said the proof, and brings up a challenge to the proof itself.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Confirming the attribution by recalling the actual conversation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought רב יוסף had wrongly connected this proof to רב יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof really was רב יהודה's, and רב יוסף even asked him a question about it.

steps.title: Holding the reins does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answered that רב and שמואל both say holding the reins does not acquire. So a rider is no different from a wagon-sitter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to me: רב and שמואל both say that holding the reins does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף reports רב יהודה's answer to the reins question. Holding the reins does not count, so the proof from the wagon still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question only worked if holding the reins could acquire. Since רב and שמואל say it cannot, the rider and the wagon-sitter really are the same. So the proof from the wagon משנה stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Holding the reins does not acquire. That is why riding can be compared to sitting in a wagon.

phrases.english: And he said to me: Rav and Shmuel
both say:
Reins do not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לִי רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reins challenge raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing the difference between the two cases by stating a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rider holds the reins, so he might acquire even though a wagon-sitter does not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Reins do not acquire, so riding is just like sitting in a wagon.

steps.title: Another version: אביי asks the reins question
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the story: here אביי himself asks רב יוסף how riding can be learned from sitting, since a rider holds the reins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: אביי said to רב יוסף: How can the master learn riding from sitting? The one sitting in the wagon does not hold the reins, but the rider holds the reins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the conversation. In this version there is no argument about who said the proof. אביי directly challenges the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is the same reins question as in step 7. This time אביי asks it of רב יוסף, instead of רב יוסף asking it of רב יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same question about the reins, told in a different version of the story.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
How can the master resolve riding from sitting?
One sitting in the wagon does not hold the reins,
one riding the animal holds the reins!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second telling of the story from steps 6-8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from the wagon-sitter to the rider
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rider holds the reins and a wagon-sitter does not, so the two cases may not be comparable.

steps.title: רב יוסף answers from אידי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רב יוסף answers that אידי taught that holding the reins does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what אידי taught: Reins do not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's reins question. In this version he quotes a teaching of אידי instead of רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is the same as in step 8: reins do not acquire, so the proof stands. Only the source changes, from רב and שמואל to a teaching of אידי.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree: holding the reins does not acquire. So riding is like sitting in a wagon, and the rider does not acquire.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Idi taught:
Reins do not acquire.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Quoting a teaching that removes the difference between the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Holding the reins might make the rider different from the wagon-sitter.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to אידי, reins do not acquire, so the proof holds.

steps.title: רב הונא: reins work from a person, not for a found item
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו quotes רב הונא: holding the reins acquires an animal from another person, but not a found animal or a convert's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: holding the reins acquires when you take the animal from another person. But for a found animal, or the property of a גר who died, it does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second statement that backs up what אידי said in step 10: holding the reins does not acquire in a case like ours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא splits the rule. When an owner hands the animal over, the reins work. But in a מציאה case, like our משנה, the reins do not acquire, which matches אידי.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (a supporting teaching)
A found object that has no owner
Property of a convert who died with no heirs, so it is ownerless

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥelbo said in the name of Rav Huna:
Holding the reins, when taking from another person, acquires.
With a found animal, or a convert's property, it does not acquire.
phrases.notes: A גר who dies with no Jewish heirs leaves his things ownerless, so anyone can grab them, just like a found item.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up אידי's rule from step 10 by giving the same ruling for found items.
steps.raayaObject: אידי's teaching that holding the reins does not acquire (in a מציאה case)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רב הונא, quoted by רבי חלבו

steps.title: What does the word מוסירה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the reins are called מוסירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are the reins called מוסירה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the meaning of the word מוסירה. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not only about vocabulary. The meaning of the word will explain why reins work from a person but not for a found item.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of the word

phrases.english: What is the meaning of the word 'moseira'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key word in רב הונא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word מוסירה, and through it, why the reins work only in some cases.

steps.title: Reins are for handing something over
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains in the name of אידי that מוסירה comes from 'handing over'. So it works only when someone hands the animal to you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: אידי explained to me that it is like a person who hands something over (מוסר) to his friend. It makes sense that from another person he acquires, because the other person hands it to him. But with a found animal or a convert's property, who is handing it to him so that he should acquire?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The word מוסירה means 'handing over', and that explains רב הונא's split ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reins are a way for a seller to pass the animal to a buyer. When there is an owner handing it over, it works. When the animal has no owner, nobody is handing anything over, so holding the reins does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that (sets up a contrast)

steps.whatToRemember: Reins (מוסירה) are a 'handing over' method. They work only when an owner gives the animal, not for a found item or ownerless property.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Idi explained to me
it is like a person who hands an item over to his friend.
phrases.notes: The word מוסירה sounds like מוסר, 'hands over'.

phrases.english: It makes sense that from another person he acquires,
since the other person hands it to him.
But with a found animal or a convert's property,
who is handing it to him, that he should acquire?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and explains the reason for רב הונא's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוסירה means 'handing over'. It works only when an owner hands the animal over, so not for a מציאה or a convert's property.

steps.title: The משנה seems to show a rider acquires
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from the משנה of two people riding an animal. It argues the משנה must follow the רבנן, so a rider acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from the משנה: 'If two were riding on an animal, etc.' Whose opinion is this? If you say רבי מאיר, now that even one sitting in a wagon acquires, do we need to say that a rider acquires? Rather, isn't it the רבנן? Learn from it that a rider acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea from steps 8-10 that a rider is no better than a wagon-sitter and does not acquire. It uses our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This relies on שמואל's switched version from step 5, where רבי מאיר holds the wagon-sitter liable, so for him even sitting counts as an act that acquires. Then a rider acquiring would be obvious, so the משנה must follow the רבנן. That means even the רבנן agree a rider acquires, which goes against the conclusion of steps 5-10.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a משנה or ברייתא)
A rider sitting on the animal
Now that (if even the weaker case works)

phrases.english: They challenged:

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: If two were riding on an animal, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה at the start of our פרק: two riding, or one riding and one leading, split the animal.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
If you say it is Rabbi Meir,
now that one sitting in a wagon acquires,
phrases.notes: This follows שמואל's switched version from step 5, where רבי מאיר is the one who holds the wagon-sitter liable.

phrases.english: do we need to say a rider does?!
Rather, isn't it the Rabbis?
And learn from it that a rider acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of whether a rider acquires, now challenging the view that he does not.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view (steps 8-10) that according to the רבנן a rider, like a wagon-sitter, does not acquire.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה would be obvious according to רבי מאיר, so it must follow the רבנן, and it says a rider acquires.

steps.title: The rider is steering with his legs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rider in the משנה is driving the animal with his legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A rider who drives the animal with his legs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The rider in the משנה acquires only because he is also moving the animal with his legs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just sitting on the animal does not acquire. But driving the animal forward counts as מנהיג, which does acquire. So the משנה does not prove that riding alone works.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows the case)
Leading or driving the animal so it moves

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
One who drives it with his legs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that just riding acquires.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rider acquires only because he drives the animal with his legs, which is a kind of מנהיג.

steps.title: Then it is the same as leading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the rider is driving the animal, he is just a מנהיג, which the משנה already mentions.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as leading!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the rider is driving the animal, why does the משנה list him separately from the one who leads?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already has a case of one riding and one leading. If the rider is also a kind of leader, it seems the משנה is repeating itself.

phrases.english: If so, that is the same as leading!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the rider is driving with his legs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Driving with the legs is just מנהיג, so the משנה would be listing the same thing twice.

steps.title: Two kinds of leading, and neither wins
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches two types of leading, to show that the rider is not stronger than the one leading by the reins.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of leading. You might have said the rider is stronger, since he is both leading the animal and holding it. So the משנה teaches us that he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה lists both kinds of leading on purpose. This closes the challenge from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the rider should get more, since he drives it and also holds it. The משנה tells us both sides are equal and they split the animal. So the משנה is not repeating itself, and it still does not prove that just riding acquires.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: The rider in the משנה acquires only because he steers with his legs. The rider and the one leading by the reins are equal, so they split the animal.

phrases.english: There are two kinds of leading.
You might have said
the rider is stronger,
since he leads it and also holds it,
so it teaches us that he is not.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why both cases are needed (a hidden חידוש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rider should get more because he leads it and also holds it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rider and the one leading are equal, and they split the animal.

steps.title: A new source: two people pulling a camel or driving a donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new proof with תא שמע and starts quoting a ברייתא about two people who pull a camel or drive a donkey together, or where one pulls and the other drives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof from a ברייתא: two people who were pulling a camel or driving a donkey together, or where one was pulling it and the other was driving it…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof by quoting the opening case of a ברייתא. The ruling has not come yet. It will come in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the normal ways people move animals. A camel is pulled from the front, and a donkey is driven from behind. It also covers a mixed case, where one person pulls and the other drives. By laying out these cases, the גמרא is preparing a source it will use for the question of whether a רוכב can acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: "Come and hear": the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
Pulling the animal toward yourself, from the front
Driving the animal forward, from behind

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the ruling yet. This line only describes the case. What these people acquire, and the proof, come in the next lines of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
two people who were pulling a camel,
or driving a donkey,
or where one was pulling
and one was driving,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the משנה about two riders in Steps 14–17, the גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, to look at the same question about acquiring an animal.
steps.raayaObject: Whether, and how, riding or leading an animal works to acquire it
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about two people pulling a camel or driving a donkey. Only the case is quoted here; the ruling comes next.
